precepts.text: But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved. See that? So Judah is the mount Zion which he loved.
precepts.point: Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. Zion right there refers to Judah. Deliver thyself, O Judah, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon, that dwellest with the so-called Caucasians, that is here in North America.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord”: the north is North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: we are scattered everywhere. Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion.” Zion right there refers to Judah.

“But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” See that? Judah is the mount Zion which he loved. So Zechariah is saying, deliver thyself, O Judah, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon, with the so-called Caucasians, here in North America.

Judah has a work to do. Moses blessed him: “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.” Judah would be the one going out to teach, to find the tribes and teach them the word of God. Not only would Judah be fighting in the system he lives in; a remnant of them would wake up, go out, teach and gather the twelve tribes of Israel. Help Judah against his enemies, against the white man.

And Jacob said: “Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies”: always struggling, always fighting, and not for no reason, but for the liberation of his people. “thy father’s children shall bow down before thee”, because Judah would be in the forefront teaching and gathering the tribes. “Judah is a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?” What happened? They gave us crack, heroin, feminism, bad education, all that the white man did to us, and Judah just rolled over and went to sleep. Now we just want money; the fight is gone. But the true liberation comes from the teachers of the Bible.

precepts.text: But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved. That is how we know the Zion dwelling with the daughter of Babylon is Judah.
precepts.point: Understand this: all Judah is not in North America, just like all Levi is not on the island of Haiti, and all Benjamin is not on Jamaica or Trinidad. Israel and Judah were scattered worldwide; Zechariah is pointing out a remnant of Judah that is in North America. And what is so special about this group here? The house of David is here. You are going to find that thing out.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord”: the land of the north is North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven.” Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Which Zion?

“But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” The Lord chose the tribe of Judah, mount Zion. So we know that the Zion dwelling with the daughter of Babylon is Judah: deliver thyself, O Judah.

Benjamin does not dwell with the daughter of Babylon; they are on a nice, pleasant island. Levi does not dwell with the daughter of Babylon. That's why all the tribes make fun of Judah: we have places to go back to when we want to run; y'all have no place to go. Why? Because Judah dwells with the daughter of Babylon, with Edom, in North America.

“For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye”: he that touches you touches my favorite. “For, behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants”: Edom shall be a spoil to us, and we are the servants here. “and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me.”

precepts.text: But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved. That is the Zion it is talking about.
precepts.point: For behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants. Write this down: the servants there is us. Right now we are their servants, but God will shake his hand upon the nations and they shall be a spoil to their servants.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Zechariah cries “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Zion is sometimes spoken of as Jerusalem the city, and sometimes as the twelve tribes. But the Psalm shows which Zion this is: the Most High “chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” That is what it is talking about.

So the Zion that dwells with the daughter of Babylon is Judah. The call just before it, “Come out of her, my people”, shows that God's people are in Babylon, and Zechariah is more specific, tribe by tribe: “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north”. The land of the north is North America. That's Babylon.

Judah is the one living here in the land of the north. Benjamin can go back to the Caribbean islands, Ephraim can go back to the Caribbean islands, Levi can go back to the Caribbean islands; it is Judah that is always here. So when the Lord says “Deliver thyself, O Zion”, he is calling the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved, out of America.

precepts.text: But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved. That is the Zion of this prophecy.
precepts.point: Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. Many scriptures make Zion the twelve tribes, but in this context Zion is Judah, and God is pinpointing the group of Judah dwelling with the daughter of Babylon in the land of the north.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “come forth, and flee from the land of the north”: flee from North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: all Israel scattered, like we read in Matthew 24 and James 1. Then he singles out one group: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.”

Many scriptures tell us that Zion represents the twelve tribes. But in this context, which Zion is it? Asaph answers: “But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” That is the Zion right there.

So “Deliver thyself, O Zion” is talking about Judah: deliver yourself, Judah. That does not mean all the Judahites are in the land of the north; Judah was dispersed like all the other tribes. But God is pinpointing a particular group of Judah that would be in the land of the north, dwelling with the daughter of Babylon.

That fits the rest of the prophecy. In these last days the Lord raises up Judah first: the Lord “shall save the tents of Judah first”, and the blessing of Judah is, “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people.” The voice of Judah is the teaching of Judah, carried to the other eleven tribes.

precepts.text: He cast out the heathen, divided them an inheritance by line and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“He cast out the heathen also before them, and divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.” He cast out the heathen before us, divided the land to the tribes by line, and set each tribe in its tents.

That is what it means for the Lord to bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents. The tents of Jacob are the tribes of Israel dwelling in their own inheritance, and to bring them again is to cast out the heathen once more and set the twelve tribes back in their inheritance.

Then Jeremiah goes on: “and the city shall be builded upon her own heap”, because that land is going to be destroyed and built again, and the tribes dwell in it again as the Lord made them to dwell at the first.

precepts.text: I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter dark sayings of old. The dark sentences are the prophecies the prophets wrote in parables about the last days. The wicked do not understand them, our people do not, but the one percent in high places do.
precepts.point: India and Pakistan have nuclear bombs. Why can Iran not have them? Because the higher-ups understand dark sentences. Many senators are confused, saying there was no imminent threat, because the people above them are the ones who understand.

note.label: The Real Reason Iran Was Attacked

precepts.why:
Daniel says that in the latter time of their kingdom “a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.” The psalm explains what dark sentences are: “I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old”.

The dark sayings of old are the prophecies the prophets wrote about. The dark sentences are the prophecies and the things the prophets spoke in parables that are going to take place in the last days, like the scriptures about the Carmanians raging.

All the wicked don't understand them. Our people don't understand them. But there is a one percent in society, the spiritual wickedness in high places, the shadow government that is really ruling, who understand them to an extent, and what they don't understand they learn from us, watching online and recording right now.

They understand that Iran, with Europe, the Arabs and all the sons of Ishmael, is going to destroy Israel and America in the future. That is why they say we cannot allow Iran to have intercontinental ballistic missiles or nuclear warheads, while India and Pakistan have nuclear bombs. Many in the US government and the senators are confused, saying there was no imminent threat, but the people above them understand. Trump ran saying he was not getting into no wars, and now he is in one, because he does not really make the decisions.

So the real reason Iran was attacked is to try to stop God's prophecies, and since they can't stop them, to slow down Bible prophecy. That king who understands dark sentences is this system here in America, in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full.

precepts.text: When he slew them, then they sought him, and they returned and enquired early after God.
precepts.point: He delivereth the poor in his affliction and openeth their ears in oppression. Affliction is the only time the people turn to God.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
Psalm 78 shows the same pattern: “Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in trouble.” The trouble is affliction. “When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned and enquired early after God.”

When God slew us. What do you see taking place all over the streets right now? Our people being oppressed, locked up, put in prison by ICE officers. Then we seek God. That is when we return and enquire early after the Lord: when bad things start happening to us.

That is why judgment must begin first at the house of the Lord. Number one, for us to turn back to our God. Number two, to prove us: as you turn to him, bad things will happen to see whether you believe and trust in him. “And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.” He is the one who will redeem us from the condition we are in.

And Isaiah 30 gives the teachers their job: though the Lord gives the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, the teachers will not be removed into a corner any more. As our people cry under the affliction, we go to them and tell them why it is happening: this is the way, walk ye in it. Not guns, as some are calling for; the word of God is what will change our people and bring destruction on this place.

precepts.text: Set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments; works means keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: All the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

precepts.why:
Works by the Bible's own dictionary is keeping his commandments: “That they might set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments”. Set your hope in God, forget not his works, but keep his commandments.

So when James says Rahab was justified by works, that is what works means. Faith without works is dead, and works is keeping the commandments. Rahab's faith showed in what she did.

precepts.text: He smote his enemies in the hinder parts, and put them to a perpetual reproach; a perpetual embarrassment for taking the ark of the Lord and sitting it beside their idol.
precepts.point: The hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods. Emerods are what we know today as hemorrhoids: swollen veins in the lower rectum that bleed and cause pain. The Most High was not playing games with the heathen; he literally afflicted them in their behinds for stealing the ark.

note.label: 1 Samuel 5: Dagon Falls Before the Ark

precepts.why:
The Psalm tells the same history in one line: “And he smote his enemies in the hinder parts: he put them to a perpetual reproach.” That is what happened at Ashdod. “the hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods.”

Emerods are what we know today as hemorrhoids: swollen veins in the lower rectum that bleed and cause pain. So when the Psalm says the hinder parts, it means exactly that. The Most High was not playing games with the heathen; he literally afflicted them in their behinds for stealing the ark.

And he put them “to a perpetual reproach”: a perpetual embarrassment, for taking the ark of the Lord and sitting it beside their idol.

precepts.text: He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds, from following the ewes great with young, to feed Jacob his people; sheep in the backyard to feeding the nation.
precepts.point: Taking a keeper of sheep and making him the shepherd of the nation is a pattern with the Most High; he took leaders and prophets from following literal flocks and set them to feed the flock of Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“He chose David also his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds: From following the ewes great with young he brought him to feed Jacob his people, and Israel his inheritance.” Sheep in the backyard to feeding the nation.

The Most High took leaders and prophets from following literal flocks and set them to feed the flock of Israel. The youngest son who kept the sheep while his brothers passed before Samuel was brought to feed Jacob.

precepts.text: A lot of people, meaning the other nations, think this Bible pertains to them, but it does not; you might find them in the Bible, but they are not of the Bible.
precepts.point: He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to make known to their children, so the generation to come and the children yet to be born might know them, declare them to their children, set their hope in God, and keep His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
“For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children”. The law was appointed in Israel, for Israel to hand down to their children, that they might set their hope in God and keep his commandments.

Ecclesiasticus says the same about the whole book: “All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high God, even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage unto the congregations of Jacob.” The law is an heritage unto the congregations of Jacob.

A lot of people, meaning the other nations, think this Bible pertains to them, but it does not. You might find them in the Bible, but they are not of the Bible. The testimony was established in Jacob and the law appointed in Israel, and it was commanded to our fathers to pass to our children.

precepts.text: The Lord will return to His place until they acknowledge their offense and seek His face; in their affliction they will seek Him early.
precepts.point: Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping His laws, statutes, and commandments. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way He wants.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
“When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned and enquired early after God.” Hosea shows this is how the Lord works with us: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Lord returns to his place until we acknowledge our offence and seek his face. In our affliction we seek him early. Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping his laws, statutes and commandments.

Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way he wants, and when he slays us we remember that God is our rock and the high God our redeemer.

precepts.text: In His mercy He led forth the people He redeemed and guided them in His strength unto His holy habitation; He is our redeemer.
precepts.point: Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping His laws, statutes, and commandments. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way He wants.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
“And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.” Moses sang of that redeemer at the Red Sea: “Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people which thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided them in thy strength unto thy holy habitation.”

In his mercy he led forth the people he redeemed and guided them in his strength unto his holy habitation. He is our redeemer. That is what our fathers remembered when he slew them and they returned and sought him early: the God who brought them out was the one they had gone off from.

precepts.text: They provoked Him to jealousy with strange gods and sacrificed unto devils, and they were unmindful of the Rock that begot them and forgot God that formed them; the Rock is the Lord.
precepts.point: Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping His laws, statutes, and commandments. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way He wants.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
Israel had to be slain before they remembered that God was their rock. Moses tells how they forgot him: “They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger. They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not. Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.”

They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods and sacrificed unto devils, and they were unmindful of the Rock that begot them and forgot God that formed them. The Rock is the Lord.

That is why he slew them, and that is why, when he did, “they remembered that God was their rock”. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way he wants, until we turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High.

precepts.text: They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.
precepts.point: Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping His laws, statutes, and commandments. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way He wants.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
Our fathers “remembered that God was their rock”. Paul tells who that Rock was in the wilderness: they “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. So the rock Israel forgot and remembered again in their affliction is Christ, the same Rock Moses said begat them. When we are slain and return to inquire early after God, it is to that Rock and redeemer that we come back.

precepts.text: He made His own people go forth like sheep and guided them like a flock; we are that flock.
precepts.point: We are that flock, the lost sheep that needs to be found by the voice, this Bible. This Bible tells us from Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 who the Israelites are that have been scattered to the four corners of the earth. That is the gospel that needs to go out to give our people praise and uplift them in their spirits.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
“For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand.” Psalm 78 shows when he made us his flock: he “made his own people to go forth like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.”

He made his own people go forth like sheep and guided them like a flock. We are that flock, the lost sheep that needs to be found by the voice, and that voice is this Bible. It tells us from Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 who the Israelites are that have been scattered to the four corners of the earth.

That is the gospel that needs to go out to give our people praise and uplift them in their spirits: he is our God, we are the sheep of his hand, and today if we will hear his voice.

precepts.text: He appointed a law in Israel commanded to our fathers, to be made known to the children so they set their hope in the Most High and keep his commandments.
precepts.point: David showed this with Saul: he cut off the skirt of Saul's robe in the cave but would not kill the Most High's anointed, and Saul confessed David was more righteous, rewarding good for evil. The coals of fire are the shame that comes on such an enemy.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

precepts.why:
Feeding the hungry enemy and giving the thirsty enemy water is a commandment, and the commandments were given to one people. “For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children: That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children: That they might set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments”.

The law was appointed in Israel and commanded to our fathers, to be made known to the children so they set their hope in the Most High and keep his commandments. It is the law among Israel, generation to generation.

That settles who the enemy of Proverbs 25:21 is. This is not our natural enemies of the other nations; it is an enemy among your own people, dealt with by the law given only to Israel and taught to our children.

precepts.text: He established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel.
precepts.point: His own are named all through the scriptures: the people the law was appointed to, and sin is the breaking of that law.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why: Who are his own? “For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children”. The law was appointed in Israel, so his own are Israel, named all through the scriptures. He came unto his own, the people the law was appointed to, and his own received him not.
